records.rationale: Retain the generic netlink multicast wrapper, C inline helpers and bindings for Rust Binder reports consumed by GrapheneOS CachedAppOptimizer. Adapt message lengths to native signed arithmetic and u16 attribute bounds; reject invalid multicast groups before transferring SKB ownership and treat listener errors as no listeners. Header sizes derive from generated native types because C size macros are not exported by bindgen. Registration and operations now expose unsafe lifetime contracts: the family must stay registered and must not race registration/unregistration. The Binder caller establishes that invariant before filesystem publication and keeps it after successful activation. These are deliberate source-API corrections, with no historical binary KMI requirement. Native LTS netlink C implementations remain byte-identical. The extracted host checks cover size/ownership failures, not real netlink traffic or concurrency.

records.rationale: Retain the Rust Binder transaction-failure and oneway-spam multicast reports, NET dependency and UAPI bindings. GrapheneOS BinderNetlink resolves the binder/report family and CachedAppOptimizer consumes error/PID/size/oneway information. Preserve the existing attribute numbering and separate spam/failure reports, optional registration when C remains active, and reply error semantics. Adapt registration/calls to explicit lifetime contracts and retain active module text after publication; native group allocation and authorization are unchanged. Reports expose transaction metadata to allowed generic-netlink listeners, not payloads; local SELinux denies generic sockets to untrusted apps and allows system_server. Runtime policy enforcement, report delivery and the wider Rust Binder implementation are not certified by this scoped decision.

records.rationale: Retain both 32-entry Rust Binder transaction-history files, matching positive GrapheneOS dumpstate consumers and binderfs SELinux labels. Per-slot spinlocks protect copying; bounded context-name copies and bounded byte-string formatting do not overread unterminated 16-byte names. Preserve signed reply handle display, failure location/errno and exclusion of pending-frozen status from the failure log. Atomic cursor wrapping and debug-id ordering intentionally provide a best-effort diagnostic ring, not a complete ordered transaction stream. Adapt initialization to prepare locally owned allocations and publish them only after all fallible registration completes; failures now release both buffers. The short interval after filesystem publication and before infallible log publication can omit initial diagnostic records, which is documented and preferable to leaking allocations on failed loads. Successful activation retains module text; inactive loads remain unloadable. Native LTS Binder implementation and access-control paths are not replaced by this optional Rust implementation.
